requirements.text: One canonical material, fingerprint, report ID, and creation request ID make exact requests idempotent while keeping distinct account, principal, title, source order, and metadata inputs distinct.

First creation requires reports:write plus mail:read.message. After an exact-replay miss that passes rolling-rate admission, it durably retains exactly one rate-ledger attempt before checking mail:read.message; missing source scope performs zero source reads, materializer invocations, report/artifact/citation/capacity-total/publication writes, but never claims zero total writes. Authorized creation then resolves every source under the configured account, obtains bounded normalized text from the production parser/promotion projection or the production-faithful legacy materializer, rejects missing, identity-only, tombstoned-only, cross-account-only, and textless identities without disclosure, and stores exact text-only evidence snapshots.

A deterministic report model uses bounded text excerpts and stable citations; only the accepted renderer creates Markdown and HTML, with no raw mail HTML, URLs, active content, filesystem path, or remote resource.

Report, artifact, source snapshot, source-link, and provenance records publish and read back in one SQLite transaction, reject UPDATE, DELETE, REPLACE, and duplicate-key INSERT, reopen intact, and ride the verified whole-database backup and empty-root restore path. The private principal rate ledger is durable admission state, not a mutable report graph.

Owner, account, scope, authorization method, body digest, creation request ID, and creation time come only from trusted server dependencies and cannot be overridden by request fields, metadata, headers, or correlation IDs.

Replay and concurrency return the first committed response exactly; replay requires reports:write but is checked before and exempt from mail:read.message, attempt-rate, report-count, logical-byte, source, and allocation admission because it performs no current-source or snapshot-text read; a collision, corruption, busy timeout, renderer rejection, or storage failure publishes no alternate or partial report.

Serving resolves report and source records by trusted owner and configured account, verifies durable digests before output, rerenders model version 1, and preserves the accepted routes, scopes, headers, and text-only boundary.

The reports create adapter uses the shared operation client and #213/#214 outcome authority; JSON is the validated response, human values are branded untrusted segments, errors keep central semantics, and the feature owns no exit number or stream.

The shared HTTP boundary enforces an operation-specific non-raiseable 1 MiB reports.create body cap after authentication and reports:write authorization but before body materialization. Policy A then caps the account at 10000 immutable committed reports and 2147483648 logical charged bytes and each authenticated principal at 10 non-replay attempts in every rolling 60000 milliseconds, with exact replay first and each admitted miss durably charged before mail:read.message authorization, no committed-record deletion or eviction, and request_too_large/413 denial without public or configuration schema widening.

Every ECMAScript string accepted by the frozen public schemas and trusted principal boundary survives identity, SQLite, reopen, restore, response serialization, and exact replay without normalization or surrogate replacement by using canonical JSON-string bytes rather than raw SQLite TEXT.

Issue 232 has an exact mutation and proof boundary, including the accepted remote-placement production caller, strict normalizedText admission, and a default-5000-millisecond focused suite with test-owned WAL cleanup and no timeout override; issue 165 retains ownership of the production-adapter and composed-CLI parity cells after consuming #232 evidence.

identityAuthority.replayRule: An existing row whose fingerprint, canonical byte material, account, owner, versions, title, metadata, ordered sources, artifact digests, and response provenance all verify returns the first committed response byte-for-value after schema serialization, before any rate/count/byte admission and without resolving current source placement or loading current/snapshot source text again.

Never select report_artifacts.model_json or report_source_snapshots.source_text_json for create replay. Those content-bearing records are verified only by their separately authorized serving routes; their durable existence and metadata, together with exact identity and response reconstruction, are sufficient for a metadata-only create replay.
identityAuthority.replayAuthorizationRule: Every invocation first passes the registered reports:write HTTP authorization. An exact committed replay then succeeds without mail:read.message or any rate-ledger/capacity operation because it reads only immutable report/link/provenance metadata and allocates nothing. If no exact report exists and rolling-rate admission succeeds, exactly one attempt is committed and retained before mail:read.message is checked. Missing source scope returns the exact insufficient_scope 403 with zero source reads, materializer invocations, report/artifact/citation/capacity-total/publication writes, while the one rate-ledger attempt remains; it is therefore never described as zero total writes.
identityAuthority.collisionRule: An occupied report ID with any non-exact identity or durable-record mismatch is corruption or a hash collision. Return redacted internal_error, emit only private bounded diagnostics, write nothing, and never mint a random or suffixed identity.
identityAuthority.concurrencyRule: A process-local identity-scoped single-flight guard serializes identical contenders before replay and capacity; the guard is removed in one finally path when its last waiter exits, so identities do not accumulate. BEGIN IMMEDIATE separately serializes principal-rate admission and account-wide publication admission. A same-identity waiter rereads and returns the winner before capacity. A busy-timeout branch returns internal_error with zero report rows; a later retry returns the winner. Duplicate guards and unique keys make a second report impossible even if another process bypasses the in-memory guard.

sourceAuthority.resolutionOrder: After an exact-replay miss and the mail:read.message guard, resolve each unique source sequentially in request order. Check canonical identity and configured-account placement before reading normalized text; stop at the first ineligible source and return the same public not_found outcome for every ineligible reason.
sourceAuthority.eligibility: The canonical messages row exists; no message_content_states identity-only row exists; at least one remote_placements row for the injected active account has tombstone_observed_at IS NULL; and message_text_projections version 1 contains a non-empty production-normalized text value. sourceAuthority.placementRule: One active placement in the configured account is sufficient even when another placement for that same account is tombstoned. Active placement only in another account is cross-account-only and ineligible.
sourceAuthority.plainSelection: The production MIME parser emits one bounded message-level normalizedText string. MailParser keeps decoded text/plain when present and, with skipHtmlToText=false plus an explicit bounded maxHtmlLengthToParse, derives text only when HTML supplies the message text. No report-only plain/HTML SQL synthesis exists.
sourceAuthority.htmlFallback: HTML-to-text conversion is owned only by the production MIME parser with its pinned dependency and limits. Report code never reads original HTML, implements a second converter, or selects HTML body blobs directly.
sourceAuthority.forbiddenContent: Report construction and source serving never directly read body blobs, original message HTML, attachments, filenames, headers, URLs, remote resources, IMAP, or the network. The sole exception is the legacy normalized-text materializer: after both scopes and configured-account eligibility, it verifies the canonical raw-EML digest/size, copies exact bytes into an owner-only stage, and invokes the same production parser; only its bounded text projection may reach report code.
sourceAuthority.snapshotRule: Parse the canonical source string from its canonical JSON BLOB, require byte-for-byte reserialization, and store that exact value once under owner, account, message ID, and projection version with a digest of its canonical string bytes and its emitted UTF-8 byte length. sourceAuthority.servingRule: After creation, the durable snapshot remains the citation source even if all remote placements later tombstone or disappear. The text route never re-resolves placement and never falls back to current raw or HTML content.
sourceAuthority.citationRule: Citation identity is the request message ID. Label is exactly Source <one-based decimal request ordinal> with no zero padding. Response citations, report-model citations, durable source links, and rendered links use the same ordered pair.

normalizedTextAuthority.futureIngestionRule: The canonical promotion transaction inserts and strict-read-backs the message_text_projections row with the message, raw-blob reference, placements, structured MIME rows, routing decisions, and journal. Failure rolls the complete promotion back.
normalizedTextAuthority.legacyMaterializerRule: For a configured-account eligible legacy canonical message with no projection, read its immutable raw-eml reference, open the canonical blob without following symlinks, verify regular-file identity, exact size, and SHA-256, copy and fsync the exact bytes into an owner-only staging file, invoke parseStagedEml with the same production configuration, atomically insert and strict-read-back the projection, and await idempotent stage cleanup. normalizedTextAuthority.materializerTransitionRule: One invocation owns cancellation and exactly one awaited idempotent cleanup barrier. Active states name current work. normalizedTextAuthority.legacyConcurrencyRule: Concurrent materializers serialize on the message/projection key. A loser exact-verifies the winner's raw digest, parser id, canonical text bytes, digest, and lengths; mismatch is corruption. INSERT OR REPLACE and mutation are forbidden.
normalizedTextAuthority.reportRule: A first create reads only the durable projection. Materialized normalized text may persist when later report rendering or publication fails because it is canonical message data, not a partial report.
normalizedTextAuthority.backupRule: The projection is in the primary SQLite database and is included by the accepted database backup. Empty-root restore plus strict reopen must reproduce the row; a legacy restored row without a projection uses the same verified materializer and raw blob.
normalizedTextAuthority.proofRule: At least one composed fixture must begin with staged RFC 5322 EML bytes, run parseStagedEml through real single-message ingestion and canonical promotion, create through real HTTP/service/SQLite, then serve matching report and text evidence after reopen. A direct-SQL-only source fixture cannot satisfy this proof. A second fixture must restore a legacy database/raw blob with no projection, run the safe materializer, and prove byte-identical text/report behavior.

transactionSteps: Validate the already parsed request, trusted context, configured single account, fixed versions, canonical string bytes, and per-request source count before acquiring an identity-scoped single-flight guard.

Compute canonical identity, report ID, and server-derived creation request ID; under the guard perform the metadata-only exact-replay lookup before any capacity, source, snapshot-text, or materializer operation.

Exact-verify and return an existing report under reports:write alone, or fail collision/corruption. On an exact-replay miss, atomically evaluate rolling-rate admission; a rate-denied miss changes no ledger or report row, while every admitted miss commits and retains exactly one principal attempt before mail:read.message authorization or source materialization.

Still before any source read, reject an account already at 10000 committed reports or 2147483648 logical charged bytes; then require mail:read.message. Missing source scope returns the frozen 403 after exactly one retained rate-ledger attempt, with zero source reads, materializer invocations, report/artifact/citation/capacity-total/publication writes, and never a zero-total-writes claim.

Resolve every first-create source from its production-normalized durable projection in request order; a legacy-safe materializer completes before the report publication transaction and may remain as canonical message data if later report work fails.
